findings.description: The requirement detects a mismatch with a stored reference, but OP-SYS-004 leaves the reference and comparison method undefined. A verifier cannot determine which program changes must cause a mismatch.
OP-SYS-006 leaves the origin and wrap behavior of the fault-report timestamp undefined, so the expected value across resets and counter wrap cannot be determined.
The required code 8 fault report includes an entity field under SYS-SUP-024, but CON-SUP-112 does not define its value for a watchdog reset.
findings.requested_change: Define the entity value for a watchdog-reset fault report after the product decision is made.

findings.description: OP-SYS-005 leaves the status state values and the meaning of fault count undefined. The expected STS response cannot be determined for a given operating and reset history.

The requirement demands detection at expiry while accepting a completion at that instant. OP-SYS-009 leaves the treatment of a completion in the same 100 µs measurement step as expiry unspecified, preventing a boundary verdict.
The requirement accepts a start at the limit and detects a start later than the limit, but OP-SYS-009 leaves unresolved how starts in the same 100 µs measurement step as expiry are distinguished.

CON-SUP-111 requires the classified reset cause to be readable by the service tool. SYS-SUP-031 only sends it in a start-up message, while SYS-SUP-033 through SYS-SUP-035 provide no request that returns it. OP-SYS-002 records the missing interface decision.
findings.requested_change: Specify how the service tool reads the classified reset cause after the interface decision is made.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 requires the fault report to be transmitted after safe-state entry. SYS-SUP-023 specifies only a 10 ms deadline from detection, and SYS-SUP-027 requires the report before reset; neither requires transmission after entry. OP-SYS-008 records the unresolved ordering and timing decision.
findings.requested_change: Specify the report ordering and compatible timing after the product decision is made.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-024 requires an entity in every fault report, but SYS-SUP-026 defines entities only for codes 1 through 7. CON-SUP-112 also defines codes 8 and 9; OP-SYS-003 records their missing entity values.
findings.requested_change: Define the entity values for fault codes 8 and 9 after the product decision is made.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-003 detects a late-start fault only when the task starts, while CON-SUP-105 measures the reaction from expiry of a timing limit. OP-SYS-010 defers the detection instant for a task that never starts, leaving the timely response to that condition unresolved.

SYS-SUP-013 withholds watchdog service during a latched safe state, while SYS-SUP-010 and SYS-SUP-012 require watchdog resets after missed service. The set does not establish that outputs remain in the safe state through those resets, although CON-SUP-110 requires the latched safe state until power-on reset.
findings.requested_change: Specify and assess the interaction of watchdog resets with the latched safe state, including output behavior throughout each reset.

findings.description: The independent-watchdog service obligation constrains only intervals between consecutive services. It does not bound the first service after reset or require any service at all, so it permits the 100 ms timeout in SYS-SUP-010 during otherwise healthy operation.
findings.requested_change: Specify the first service and continuing service obligations needed to prevent independent-watchdog timeout during healthy operation.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-021 drives the status signal high whenever no fault is currently detected and the latch is clear. After a transient fault clears but before reset, this can conflict with the safe-state recovery sequence in STK-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-110, while SYS-SUP-013 continues to treat the fault as active until reset.
findings.requested_change: Define the status signal behavior from fault detection through reset consistently with the safe-state recovery sequence.
